Common misconception. Large breed dogs require less exercise (in terms of time spent exercising) due to how much they work to keep their bodies going as well as the fact they burn such larger volumes of energy when exercising.

Not a hard rule though- my 10lb dog is happy to nap and sit on your lap all day whereas my 50lb dog is non-stop hyper all day. 10lb is a Chihuahua-Border Terrier mix and the 50lb is a Boxer-Lab-Pit mix.

I think aspca says 4 hours is max to leave alone. My sister's dog used to always have somebody home, was a bichon, great dog. When her and her fiance changed schedules and atarted leaving the dog alone for 8 -10hrs it became catatonic, unresponsive, and depressed. It developed hip problems. It was sad.

Dogs are incredibly social pack animals by nature. They need a lot of attention. This is what makes them awesome family pets, but terrible bachelor pets. Dogs will get depressed and suffer all kinds of horrible ailments if you leave them alone too long. It's simply cruel.

However it's not all bad news! There are a lot of organisations that organise you to walk peoples dogs when the owners are unable to do it themselves. You could walk a dog frequently, really get to know it and love it, but you don't need to be there for it all the time. If you search you'll most likely be able to find s local organisation and find yourself a dog to walk and take care of :)
If you are gone for so long, you might want to consider getting a cat instead.
